text.p: Electric utility rate reductions could occur in Pennsylvania's transition to customer choice by the adoption of a concept known as "rate reduction bonds," PECO Energy Co chief executive Corbin A. McNeill, Jr. McNeill said.

"These bonds allow electric utilities to refinance investments in a way that provides savings to the utility that can be passed on to customers in the form of lower rates," he told a breakfast meeting of Chester County, Pa., business and political leaders.

Stating "I want to emphasize that PECO Energy supports customer choice," he said "We support a transition to electric retail competition and the opportunity for all customers to choose their electric supplier.
"And we support real and meaningful customer rate reductions" supported by cost savings such as those provided by rate reduction bonds, McNeill said.
He said the bonds, financed by an independent financial entity, would enable the utility to reduce the size of its balance sheet by retiring debt and buying back stock.
McNeill emphasized that the bonds would not be obligations of the Commonwealth.
"It is important to understand," McNeill said, that this type of financing is not new and has been used in other states by electric utilities for various purposes."

For this mechanism to be used in Pennsylvania, he said, specific statutory language would be needed both to authorize the establishment of the process and to obligate present and future Public Utility Commissions to provide adequate revenues for debt service payments associated with the bonds.
"At first glance, this may seem complicated," McNeill said, "but it is really quite simple. It takes away the issue of stranded investment, while providing customers with immediate rate reductions.

"Properly and fairly designed," he said, "we believe competition can enhance long-term economic development and produce benefits for all customers without harming utility investors or the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania."
